TextBlock.Text: South Atlantic 1982 - Argentina
Your command
Lead the Argentine fleet and air forces from the South Georgia operation to the battle for San Carlos. Your ships, submarines and aircraft form a persistent force across connected missions.

Historical Reinforcements mode delivers the campaign's scheduled reinforcement waves. Points Based mode lets you build your own force from the units available in the theater. Choose Unrestricted at campaign setup if you want access to units outside the campaign roster.
Command and survival

This campaign has no overall flagship survival requirement. Losing a carrier or a formation leader does not automatically end the campaign. Individual missions can still require a particular ship to survive or reach a withdrawal area. Read those objectives before committing your force.
Before each operation
Read the mission briefing, check the required forces, and assign suitable task forces to the deployment zones. Check aircraft assignments, available flights and remaining weapons before launching.
Review ships away for repair or rearm and their return dates. A ship still undergoing service is unavailable for missions taking place before its return.
Plan for the whole campaign
Losses, damage, ammunition expenditure and surviving crews affect later operations. Preserve scarce aircraft and specialist ships. Enemy losses also shape the forces you face later.
Optional missions have limited windows, and advancing the main campaign can close and skip an unfinished side mission. Save regularly, especially before advancing.
Campaign outcome

Sinking both British carriers wins the campaign at any point. If the British attempt to land at San Carlos, you can also win by sinking enough of their amphibious lift to prevent the landing operation from succeeding. The final operation can otherwise end in a negotiated settlement or defeat. Read its briefing for the required objectives.
Reinforcements and Task Forces
Historical Reinforcements
Ships, submarines and aircraft arrive in reinforcement packages as the campaign advances. Packages may arrive as formed task groups or as individual units in Reserve.
This mode does not use campaign points to purchase units. Replacement forces depend on the campaign's reinforcement schedule.
Points Based
Use Task Force Builder to buy units from the roster available for the selected mission. Purchases spend campaign points and must respect the force cap and mission requirements.
Mission completion can award additional points and increase the force cap. Difficulty changes starting resources, rewards, crew proficiency and whether purchased ships include their aircraft.
Check the aircraft included with each purchase. Helicopters cost points but do not consume the fleet cap. There is no national purchase discount in this campaign.
Task forces and Reserve
Organise your force into separate task groups and move units between groups and Reserve as required. Reserve is a holding pool, not an additional deployed task group.

Each mission sets its own limits on ships, submarines and task forces. Drag and drop ships into the deployment zones on the campaign map to deploy them. Deployment zones can restrict ship types and require a carrier or another specific role.
Aircraft and Submarine Operations
Embarked aircraft
Assign aircraft to compatible ships and check hangar capacity before deployment. Aircraft availability and losses carry forward with the campaign force.
Use the Starting Airborne Flights options offered by the selected mission to prepare eligible flights. Each flight must satisfy its aircraft-type, loadout and role restrictions.
Land-based aircraft

Mainland and island airbases hold finite aircraft inventories. New allocations become available as the campaign advances in both acquisition modes. Aircraft lost on a sortie reduce the force available for later operations.

Select eligible shore-based aircraft for the mission's available flights. Check the source base, aircraft numbers and loadouts. For airbases present in the tactical mission, review aircraft preparation and remaining ammunition before launch.
Shore-based and embarked aircraft have separate inventories. Aircraft transfers between campaign airbases are disabled. Check where each reinforcement arrives before planning to use it.
Exocet supply

At campaign setup, choose either the historical stock of five air-launched AM39 Exocets or a stock of 100 missiles at Río Grande. Both choices are finite, and the setting cannot be changed after the campaign begins. Check the airbase's remaining stock before assigning Super Étendard strikes.
Stanley reinforcement

Later in the campaign, you will have an opportunity to reinforce Stanley and improve its runway. Delivering the necessary supplies will allow a small force of strike aircraft to operate directly from Stanley, avoiding the long and hazardous flight from the mainland.
Optional submarine operations
Submarine missions use their own deployment requirements and can alter later operations. Check their availability before advancing the main campaign.
Keeping the Task Force in Action
Repair and rearm
Surface ships use Puerto Belgrano for service. Submarines use Mar del Plata. Sending a unit for repair or rearm removes it from operations until its stated return date.

Light, moderate and heavy damage can be repaired. At Moderate difficulty, repairs take 5, 10 and 30 campaign days respectively. Easy halves these durations, rounded up to whole days. Difficult multiplies them by 1.5, also rounded up.
Timed repairs cost no campaign points in either acquisition mode. Ships return fully repaired and rearmed. Heavy repairs can keep a ship out of action for much of the remaining campaign.

A separate rearm visit includes the outward and return passages at 20 knots and a 24-hour loading cycle. Check the total time away and return date before sending a ship. The current campaign also provides automatic rearm for deployed ships when entering Night in the Sound, RFA Raid and The Outer Picket Station. This does not replenish the entire fleet or the shore-based Exocet stock.
Losses and replacements

A ship lost in combat provides no points refund. In Points Based mode, dismissing a unit or decommissioning a heavily damaged unit returns only part of its value, according to the selected difficulty.
Reinforcements and newly available purchases do not restore aircraft already lost. Check both the surviving air group and the next mission's requirements.
Rescue and experience
Recover survivors with suitable ships or helicopters when conditions permit. In Points Based mode, every 10 survivors rescued earns one campaign point at mission end.
Crews improve their proficiency by surviving missions. Keeping experienced units in action strengthens the force for later operations.
Commander and Campaign Awards
Argentine naval command
The campaign begins with an Argentine naval commander, with Juan José Lombardo as the default name. The Service Record tracks campaign progress, combat results, losses and rescues.
Reading your awards
Select a ribbon in the Service Record to read its award record. The citations are campaign adaptations tied to your results.
Unit Prices
Reference prices for the campaign roster. Actual purchase availability depends on the selected mission and acquisition setting. Select a class name to open its unit reference.

Expect a different kind of campaign. Small forces, shared weapons and limited resources make every engagement costly.

Run.Text: Britain excels at anti-submarine warfare. Argentina has a varied fleet, but many ships are Second World War veterans with weak air defenses.
Neither side has supercarriers or massed long-range missile salvos. Small carrier air groups cannot cover everything.
Both fleets carry Exocet. British Type 42s and Argentine Hércules-class destroyers also share Sea Dart.
Historical supply gives your Super Étendards just five Exocets. Identify valuable targets before committing them.
Most strikes require low-flying Skyhawks and Daggers to deliver unguided bombs at close range. Plan the approach and escape.
A deadly combination against your strike aircraft. Avoid fighter patrols and preserve your bombers for attacks on ships.
Broadsword-class frigates provide potent but short-range defense. Avoid their coverage when planning bombing runs.
British nuclear submarines have superior speed and endurance. Use San Luis’s quiet running for ambushes and handle the elderly Santa Fe cautiously.
Long mainland flights limit available aircraft. Coordinate attacks, watch fuel and preserve your force for later operations.
